summary: This resolution sets House floor procedures for debating and amending five measures—an agriculture programs reauthorization bill, a parental-consent requirement for school gender-marker changes, the FY2026 budget resolution, a bill correcting Jewish servicemembers’ overseas graves, and an ethanol fuel waiver—by waiving points of order, limiting debate and amendments, and dictating final passage votes.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely procedural, setting debate rules for multiple bills including a farm bill (H.R. 7567) and a budget resolution (S. Con. Res. 33). It contains no substantive provisions altering spending levels or appropriations, so it has no bearing on government spending.
The resolution text makes no reference to tax policy, rates, or reforms. It is limited to procedural rules for floor consideration of unrelated measures.
No provisions in the resolution address healthcare access, funding, regulation, or market structures.
The resolution does not engage with firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues in any way.
No immigration-related content appears in the resolution.
The resolution contains no language concerning reproductive rights or abortion policy.
While one bill referenced (S. 1318) involves military cemeteries, the resolution itself is only a procedural vehicle and does not alter defense spending or policy.
H.R. 1346 (ethanol waiver under the Clean Air Act) is made in order, but the resolution itself makes no substantive change to environmental regulations.
No provisions affect welfare programs, entitlements, or safety-net funding.
The resolution facilitates consideration of H.R. 2616 (parental consent on gender markers in schools), but as a procedural measure it does not itself enact education policy.
The resolution has no connection to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related matters.
No criminal justice reforms, sentencing, or policing provisions are present.
The resolution does not address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The budget resolution (S. Con. Res. 33) is made in order, yet the rules package itself contains no debt or deficit provisions.

H.R. 2616 (requiring parental consent for gender-related changes in schools) is scheduled for consideration, but the resolution is strictly procedural and does not itself expand or limit LGBTQ protections.
No foreign aid provisions appear in the resolution.
The resolution does not address voting access, election integrity, or related reforms.
No technology, data privacy, or regulatory oversight language is included.
The resolution contains no labor, union, or employment provisions.
S. 1318 (Jewish servicemembers' grave markers) is made in order, but the resolution itself does not alter religious liberty or anti-discrimination policy.
